messages:
marisa: Quick one — after the EU-W2 network flaps last week, I ran a couple sims and p99 latency is sensitive to queue depth. need to pick a hard queue cap for the gpu pool that keeps p99 <= 450ms but doesn't blow our GPU hours budget (target 42k/mo). anyone want to sanity-check my math?

otto: share the sim inputs pls — arrival distribution, service mean, batch size assumptions.

kai: short answer: p99 is dominated by rare long tails (network retries + slow kernels). queue depth helps but only to a point.

marisa: inputs: avg qps=420, peak 2-min burst=1400, service time mean (per request) = 18ms on an A100 baseline with batching disabled for low-latency flows. target SLO p95=120ms, p99=450ms. currently we have queue_depth=128 per node, 24 nodes in eu-w2 pool.

jane: hmm. do you model arrivals as poisson or with measured burst autocorrelation? poisson underestimates burstiness.

marisa: used measured inter-arrival from last 30 days (empirical). also ran a poisson run for sanity. both show similar tail shape during the 3 high-traffic incidents.

otto: can you paste the little script/approx? even a back-of-envelope is fine.

marisa: here's the simplified model i used:

```
# inputs
lambda_peak = 1400/120.0   # requests per second (2-min burst -> rps)
mu = 1/0.018               # service per second
servers = 24
Q = 128                    # per-node queue depth
# approximate M/M/c/K style blocking -> compute utilization rho = lambda/(c*mu)
```

marisa: then i did a quick Monte Carlo with empirical inter-arrival + measured service variance, tracked response times, and varied queue depth. result: p99 drops from ~920ms at Q=512 to ~410ms at Q=96, but GPU hours increase ~6% when we push to smaller Q because admission causes retries to spill to dedicated burst pool which runs hotter.

anil: so admission control helps tail but can increase cost due to fallback to dedicated instances? that matches intuition. can we do tiering: small queue for low-priority flows, larger for SLO-critical?

marisa: that's the idea. proposed policy: SLO-critical routes keep Q=96, non-critical allow Q=256. fallback policy -> short-circuit to dedicated burst (higher cost) only if we've exhausted region headroom.

otto: two checks: 1) verify your monte carlo includes KV cache hits (those are much cheaper); 2) network retry amplification — when requests are admitted then retried, they add extra load, so admission reduces the retries but increases direct misses to dedicated.

kai: also factor cold-starts for rare model variants in eu-w2 — those add ~120ms tail when they happen concurrently. if those coincide with bursts, p99 spikes. Consider pre-warming one node for the variant during predicted busy windows.

jane: for the cost side: can you compute incremental GPU-hours vs p99 improvement per 1% budget change? I want a metric like delta_p99_per_gpu_hour.

marisa: i mocked that: going from total 40k->42k GPU-hours (5% increase) buys us p99 improvement ~100-120ms in the worst-case sim. so ~20-25ms p99 per 1% extra GPU-hours.

anil: that's a useful lever. product might accept a 3% bump if we can avoid user-visible errors. get approval?

marisa: flagged in the capacity ticket. @sre-bot can you attach last week's incident window and the sim logs to the ticket? ticket #INF-2384 referenced.

sre-bot: Incident window and sim artifacts uploaded to INF-2384: https://internal.redwood/INF-2384/artifacts :thumbsup:

otto: final suggestion: set soft Q cap = 96 with aggressive backpressure (429 + Retry-After) for SLO-critical, soft Q=240 for best-effort. route overflow to eu-w2-dedicated-burst, but add circuit breaker: if burst dedicated is >70% then reject with degradation instead of spinning up more GPUs.

marisa: thanks — i'll update the rollout doc with the numbers and a rollout play: canary on 5 nodes eu-w2, monitor p95/p99 and GPU-hours for 3h, then ramp.

kai: please add a short eval prompt set to track quality regressions — if admission causes more retries and different tokenization patterns, we should catch it.

marisa: noted. i'll paste the canary config here once ready. thanks all :)
